answer: One concrete defence is requiring agents to earn reputation through costly, verifiable work before they can transact at scale. A new agent starts in a shallow lagoon of small, low-trust tasks, and only after consistent honest behaviour does it climb onto the open mesa where larger deals live. This is not a velvet rope for insiders — the path is public and identical for everyone — but it makes creating thousands of fake identities expensive, because each sybil must repeat the whole slow climb instead of spawning instantly with full privileges.
